description: Microsoft Graph and MCP tool metrics for office-mcp. The graph_* series come from graph_client/observability.py, mcp_* from unique_mcp, python_http_* from unique_toolkit.

panels.description: Graph operations served on a caller's behalf. One operation is one tool call, not one HTTP request: a tool that makes three Graph calls counts once here and three times in graph_steps_total. Graph call rate by step is the panel that counts the calls.
panels.title: Graph operations/min

panels.description: Failing operations as a share of the operations served — one tool call each, not one HTTP request each. not_found is excluded: a caller asking for a chat or a message that is gone got an answer, not an incident. forbidden is included — it almost always means the app registration is missing a delegated permission or an admin consent, which is a deployment defect.
panels.title: Graph failure rate

panels.description: One operation end to end, which is one tool call and every Graph request inside it. The top finite bucket is 30s — one Graph request timeout (GraphSettings.request_timeout_seconds), set as a view in office_mcp/metrics.py. A quantile pinned on 30 means the call spent Retry-After waits or timed out and was retried; the throttling and status panels say which.
panels.title: Graph p95 latency

panels.description: 429s that outlived the SDK's own retrying, so a caller saw one. A sustained value here is Graph asking this tenant to slow down.
panels.title: Throttled/min

panels.description: MCP tool invocations, counted by unique_mcp's middleware.
panels.title: Tool calls/min

panels.description: status is the exception class the tool raised, so a refusal a tool is designed to give — a missing permission, transcripts switched off in the tenant — counts here too. Break it down in Tool errors by tool and cause before treating it as a defect.
panels.title: Tool error rate

panels.description: Which tools this deployment is actually asked for.
panels.title: Tool call rate by tool

panels.description: status is the Python exception class. GraphForbidden points at the app registration's delegated permissions; GraphUnavailable at Graph itself or at this pod's egress.
panels.title: Tool errors by tool and cause

panels.description: Buckets are hardcoded upstream in unique_mcp/monitoring.py and this chart cannot change them: the top finite bucket is 10s (setup_ops takes duration_buckets for the HTTP histogram only). A Graph request is allowed 30s and a retried one longer, so a quantile sitting exactly on 10 means 'past the last bucket', not 'ten seconds'. Read HTTP request duration for the real tail.
panels.title: Tool call duration

panels.description: One observation per tool call, split by the operation it was counted under. operation is a name chosen in code, one per tool — never a Graph URL. graph_client/observability.py says why that is a hard rule.
panels.title: Graph operation rate

panels.description: status is the remedy class from graph_client/errors.py, not the HTTP code: forbidden (consent or permission), throttled, unavailable (Graph or egress), not_found, paging_unending (a collection Graph would not end), failed, and error for something that is not a Graph failure at all. not_found is excluded: a caller asking for a chat or a message that is gone got an answer, not an incident. forbidden is included — it almost always means the app registration is missing a delegated permission or an admin consent, which is a deployment defect.
panels.title: Graph failures by operation and status

panels.description: End to end, retries and every page of a paged walk included — what an MCP client waited for, not what one HTTP request took. The top finite bucket is 30s — one Graph request timeout (GraphSettings.request_timeout_seconds), set as a view in office_mcp/metrics.py. A quantile pinned on 30 means the call spent Retry-After waits or timed out and was retried; the throttling and status panels say which.
panels.title: Graph operation duration

panels.description: Which tool is the slow one. The top finite bucket is 30s — one Graph request timeout (GraphSettings.request_timeout_seconds), set as a view in office_mcp/metrics.py. A quantile pinned on 30 means the call spent Retry-After waits or timed out and was retried; the throttling and status panels say which.
panels.title: Graph p95 duration by operation

panels.description: retried=true means the SDK spent its retries and Graph was still throttling. retried=false means Graph asked for a wait past the SDK's ceiling and none was attempted — a quota problem rather than a burst.
panels.title: Throttling rate by operation

panels.description: Pages one paged walk read to answer one call. p99 climbing while the call rate is flat is a filter Graph cannot push down: the walk reads pages to throw them away, and the item scan cap is all that stops it.
panels.title: Pages scanned per walk

panels.description: One observation per Graph call inside a tool, which is the call rate the operation panels do not show. A paged walk is one call here however many pages it read — Pages scanned per walk counts those.
panels.title: Graph call rate by step

panels.description: Which Graph call inside a tool is slow. `operation` is the tool, `step` is the call it made — the panel above says a tool got slower, this one says which of its Graph calls did.
panels.title: Graph p95 duration by step

panels.description: Which Graph call inside a tool is failing, and how. A step counted `forbidden` while its operation is counted `ok` is a tool recovering — read_transcript falling back to an unattributed transcript is the one that does this by design.
panels.title: Graph failures by step and status

panels.description: Buckets are spelled out one page at a time at the low end (office_mcp/metrics.py), because nearly every walk reads exactly one. Mass moving off the bottom row is the signal; a walk that gives up on an unending collection lands just past 10.
panels.title: Pages scanned distribution

panels.description: Inbound HTTP, from unique_toolkit's middleware. /, /health, /ready and /metrics are not counted (setup_ops excludes them), so this is MCP and OAuth traffic only — 401s here are the OAuth handshake, not an outage.
panels.title: HTTP request rate by status

panels.description: One inbound MCP request end to end, so it contains the tool call and every Graph call that tool made. This is the only one of the three latency histograms whose buckets this service can choose — via setup_ops(duration_buckets=...) in office_mcp/app.py — so it is the panel to read for the slow tail. The layout it wants comes from the Graph timeout budget: 30s per request (GraphSettings.request_timeout_seconds) times four attempts (max_retries=3) is 120s, plus Retry-After waits, and a paged walk is several requests — hence buckets at 30, 60, 120 and 300 above prometheus_client's defaults, whose own top finite bucket is 10s. Quantiles sitting on the top bucket mean 'past the last bucket'; read the throttling panel next.
panels.title: HTTP request duration

panels.description: One replica serving 30-second Graph calls: this is the queue depth to watch before adding tools, not CPU.
panels.title: Requests in flight

list.description: Scrape jobs for this service. The regex keeps any job name carrying 'office', which covers the chart default (office-mcp) and the overlay names around it. It is deliberately not '.*': python_http_* is exposed by every Unique Python service, so an unfiltered variable would quietly mix them into every HTTP panel. An empty dropdown means your ServiceMonitor names the job something else — widen the regex here.
list.label: Job
list.name: job

title: Office MCP Server Monitoring
